practices.title: Keep AGENTS.md within the harness's budget
Test AI-generated code more thoroughly, not less
Confine `any` to the decoded boundary
Assert what a function assumes and what it promises
A baseline is a ratchet, not a wall — and not a place to hide new debt
Make the CI check a required status check
Say why, not what
The threshold reports, the rule gates — and a legacy hotspot gets a documented ceiling
Validate config at startup, and never commit environment-specific values
Word the pointer so the agent reaches the material
Ignore a file only when the runner cannot execute it
Coverage is not verification
Triage dead code in fix order, and keep an export only through an auditable mechanism
Decode external data at the boundary, then trust the type
A deep module hides real work behind a simple interface
Reshape the interface instead of adding a handler
Write the commit message for the reader who arrives via git blame
Do not cache what the environment already says
An equivalent mutant is a decision, not a survivor
Classify an error before you write a handler
Quarantine, root-cause, eliminate — never retry
Format on write locally, check only in CI
Keep a reformat out of a logic commit
Exclude generated files from the formatter's file set
Put the doc where the harness looks
Decide whether the hook fixes and re-stages, or fails
Put a gate in pre-commit only if it is fast
Run the hook's gates serially unless they are independent
Treat every client-side hook as skippable
Delete an instruction the model already obeys
Auto-fix what the tool can fix
Fix, suppress, or record — never ignore
Enable a rule only when its report is actionable
Severity is a switch, not a dial
A suppression explains itself
Relax in tests only what tests make meaningless
